thread:
maya: Heads-up: observed steady session-cache growth (~3.5GB over 48h) on streaming toolloop workload in ded-2 canary. Not a classic leak — looks like eviction 'ripple' / stale epoch tags causing pages to be retained. :thinking:
liam: repro steps? which build + config?
maya: repro command I used:
```
# run 48h toolloop harness
./tools/run_toolloop --model redwood-v2 --mode streaming --session-len 20000 --batch=32 --kernel-selector=auto --kv-policy=adaptive
```
commit: a1b2c3d 2026-03-14, runtime flags: kernel_fallback=on, opportunistic_batching=1
sasha: saw something similar last week but tied to opportunistic batching kicking in when average seq_len > 1024. flamegraph showed lots of "pagewalk()" and "dec_ref()" hotspots instead of forward generation.
zane: grabbing logs from canary now — there's a repeating pattern where eviction scan runs but sees refs >0 and re-queues page for another pass. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:22:11Z] evict_scan: bucket=34 scanned=512 kept=13 requeue=499
[2026-03-15T09:22:11Z] pagewalk: page=0x7f9a3b refcnt=2 owner=session-8734
[2026-03-15T09:22:11Z] fallback: kernel_selector -> fallback_fastpath (latency=1.8ms)
```
maya: quick experiment: set KV_EVICT_MAX_AGE=30m and growth stops, but p99 latency increases by ~12%. numbers: baseline mem delta +3.5GB/48h -> with 30m age -> +0.1GB/48h. latency p99: 110ms -> 123ms.
liam: interesting — suggests pages are being kept due to stale epoch tag rather than actual active usage. any evidence of epoch bump not occurring after kernel fallback?
sasha: I reproduced with perf build and collected alloc profile. flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/redwood/flows/5205559001 (internal) — main stack tops are:
  - pagewalk
  - session_kv_hold
  - opportunistic_batch_apply
  - kernel_selector_fallback
This implies the batching heuristic is holding onto KV ranges while fallback churns kernels.
maya: dump from /proc/memmap shows many small fragments allocated then not freed until TTL. fragmentation metric: free_frag_ratio ~0.17 -> 0.33 over 48h.
zane: adding to this, in logs I see repeated partial releases where refcnt decremented from 3->2, 2->1 but never zero because another worker rebinds the page before final dec. race between eviction and reuse.
liam: hypothesis: opportunistic batching groups requests and pins prefix ranges longer; when kernel_selector falls back we re-route into a codepath that doesn't emit an epoch bump or doesn't decrement the session_token, so eviction sees a phantom ref.
maya: short mitigation: forcing kernel_selector=preferred_fastpath and small batch sizes stops growth but hurts throughput ~8%.
sasha: plan proposal:
  1) add explicit epoch bump / release in kernel_fallback path (hotfix candidate)
  2) add extra decrement in pagewalk when requeue happens (safety net)
  3) add CI perf test: long streaming session 72h emulation with opportunistic_batching=1 and measure mem delta (<200MB)

liam: can we get a quick microtest to reproduce deterministically? I can wire one into infra perf harness.
maya: yes, I made a repro script that simulates two interleaved workers fighting for the same prefix; will attach gist in the bug: BUG-2026-1125. gist snippet:
```
# simulate race
worker_a: read prefix A -> pin -> sleep(50ms) -> release
worker_b: read prefix A -> pin -> fallback kernel -> rebind -> release
```
This reproduces refcnt hang in ~30s locally.
zane: ops-bot reports canary deploys around the time the pattern started: ops-bot: "deploy: service/redwood-runtime canary v2026-03-14T21:10 -> success". tagging deploy in timeline.
ops-bot: deploy 2026-03-14T21:10 succeeded on ded-2 canary :white_check_mark:

maya: next steps: Sasha will own the kernel_fallback epoch bump patch, Li am will add perf test in CI, Zane will add an eviction regression alert to console (mem delta >500MB/24h -> pagewalk snapshot). I'll run a 72h canary with KV_EVICT_MAX_AGE=15m as a temporary guard.
sasha: ack — will open PR today and include unit to validate dec_ref path.
liam: I'll add the long-run job and alert. Ping me if you want me to run the 72h locally.
maya: thanks folks. tagging @eng-sre to watch canary. :mag:
zane: putting timeline note in BUG-2026-1125 and linking logs.
